content:
The 2011-12 Harvard Crimson men's basketball team was coached by Tommy Amaker and captained by Oliver McNally and Keith Wright. They finished the season with a record of 26-5, including a perfect 14-0 record in Ivy League play. This marked the first time in Harvard's history that they had won the Ivy League championship outright and clinched a spot in the NCAA Tournament.

The team was led by a balanced scoring attack, with four players averaging double figures in points per game. Keith Wright was the team's leading scorer and rebounder, averaging 10.9 points and 8.1 rebounds per game. Laurent Rivard was the team's sharpshooter, leading the team in three-point shooting percentage at 42.2%.

In the NCAA Tournament, Harvard faced off against Vanderbilt in the second round. Despite putting up a tough fight, the Crimson ultimately fell to the higher-seeded Commodores, ending their season with a 79-70 loss.

Overall, the 2011-12 Harvard Crimson men's basketball team had a historic season, setting a new standard of success for the program and earning national recognition for their achievements.
